tells.1: Flattened, over-smoothed phrasing ('Our crews did that work, in summer heat and winter cold') loses the warmth a person would bring to a thank-you
tells.3: Stock intensifiers ('blazing heat and freezing cold', 'every single install', 'lasting career') plus an exclamation point make it read as generic promotional copy
tells.4: Colon-driven compression ('The number is our members' too:', 'program: 12 spots, paid training...') crams the members' thank-you into the crew paragraph and reads like a condensed summary
tells.5: Mild parallel framing ('That number belongs to... It also belongs to...'), though it reads as deliberate rhetoric rather than filler

reason: Version 5 has the most natural voice: clear credit to crews and members, a punchy fragment list for the apprenticeship details, and no hype. Version 3 leans on stock intensifiers, and Version 4 merges the two thank-yous into one cramped paragraph.
